description: Make Gemini episode consolidation an independent background task: no model/network call under _turn_buffer_lock or any chat-reachable lock; snapshot -> Gemini outside locks -> persist episode -> trim buffer by turn ids; strict mode keeps turns and retries with backoff on failure; hard timeout; single flight; defer while a user turn is active; logging; rollup failure detail. Independent of FEAT-003 (can run in either order after FEAT-001). Requires FEAT-001's baseline.
steps: Read plan.md (sections 1, 2 item 2, 4, 5) and context.json first. If FEAT-001 findings say the hypothesis was refuted, adapt the steps to the real blocking lock before editing.

Default behaviour unchanged.

src/memory/living_user/gemini_adapter.py: summarize_episode(payload, *, timeout=None) -> _generate_json(..., timeout) -> create_chat_completion(timeout=...). Replace 'with _LANE_LOCK, inference_context(...)' with a bounded _LANE_LOCK.acquire(timeout=deadline) (CuratorInferenceError('lane_busy') on failure), HTTP read timeout = remaining budget (min 1s), release in finally.

src/memory/living_user/service.py: add config fields + env (episode_timeout_sec 60, episode_retry_sec 60, episode_fallback_rows 40, lock_wait_warn_ms 250, capture_lock_timeout_sec 2.0); module logger; _timed_buffer_lock; rewrite record_conversation_turn (no model work in lock, then request_consolidation for session change / 28-row checkpoint with keep_tail=4); bounded lock acquire in capture_interpretation_context (fallback to empty turns on timeout); request_consolidation + lazily started daemon worker 'ERIS-LivingUserEpisode' (5s poll, backoff, user_turn_active gate with overridable attribute); _take_snapshot_locked (contiguous same-session run with >=2 rows, keep_tail only for last run); _consolidate_once (non-blocking _cons_run_lock; build outside locks via _run_with_deadline(timeout+5); episode_store.add; then trim by ids under the lock; then optional dream via _dream_saved); strict failure path (no episode, buffer untouched, failures+=1, next_at=min(600, retry*2**(n-1))); pressure/no-adapter fallback rule; trace_journal.append('episode_consolidation', ...) and logger lines with lock_wait_ms, gemini_ms, duration_ms, episode_id, attempt, error; consolidation_status(); stop_consolidation(); keep flush_session() as a synchronous wrapper over _consolidate_once(strict=False); dream() requests consolidation instead of flushing inline; remove _flush_buffer_locked after grepping for references.
src/memory/living_user/episode_rollup.py: add detail=str(exc)[:160] to the failed result and a single logger warning in run()'s except block.
.env.example: add the ERIS_LIVING_USER_EPISODE_* / LOCK knobs next to the ERIS_MEMORY_GEMINI_* block. Do not edit .env.

Create src/tests/test_living_user_async_consolidation.py with fakes (no network): hot path (capture_interpretation_context, record_conversation_turn) returns <0.5s while a slow summarize_episode runs; turns recorded during the call are kept and only the snapshot ids are trimmed; episode is persisted before the buffer trim (assert via patched _save_turn_buffer_locked); failing adapter leaves buffer and episode store unchanged, failures==1, next retry in the future, no heuristic episode; hanging adapter hits the hard timeout (episode_timeout_sec small); two requests while running produce one adapter call; gate=True produces zero adapter calls; buffer >= fallback rows with failing adapter persists a heuristic episode with source_turns; model_adapter=None still produces the heuristic episode; EpisodeRollupStore.run with an invalid-segments adapter returns status failed, error ValueError and a non-empty detail; legacy flush_session() still returns an episode. Use a wait_until(condition, timeout) polling helper and call stop_consolidation() in teardown.
acceptance_criteria: No code path holds _turn_buffer_lock (or episode_store.lock) while calling summarize_episode / any model or network call.

capture_interpretation_context and record_conversation_turn return in well under 1 s while a fake summarize_episode sleeps 5-10 s (verified by the new tests and by verify script check 1 --phase after).
Turns that arrive during the Gemini call remain in the buffer; the episode is persisted (reloadable from disk) before the buffer is trimmed, and only snapshot ids are removed.

A failing or timing-out adapter leaves the buffer intact, writes no episode (except the documented pressure / no-adapter fallback), records failure in logs and living_user_trace.jsonl, and schedules a retry with exponential backoff capped at 600 s.
At most one consolidation runs at a time; no consolidation runs while GLOBAL_INFERENCE_BROKER.user_turn_active() is true.
Logs and trace events include start/end, duration, turn_buffer lock wait, Gemini duration, persisted episode id and failures.
EpisodeRollupStore failure results include a detail string.
Existing living-user tests still pass except the 2 known pre-existing failures in test_living_user_memory_v39.py.

CONFIG / ENV (LivingUserMemoryConfig, read in from_env, documented in .env.example next to ERIS_MEMORY_GEMINI_*): episode_timeout_sec <- ERIS_LIVING_USER_EPISODE_TIMEOUT_SEC (60); episode_retry_sec <- ERIS_LIVING_USER_EPISODE_RETRY_SEC (60); episode_fallback_rows <- ERIS_LIVING_USER_EPISODE_FALLBACK_ROWS (40); lock_wait_warn_ms <- ERIS_LIVING_USER_LOCK_WARN_MS (250); capture_lock_timeout_sec <- ERIS_LIVING_USER_CAPTURE_LOCK_SEC (2.0).

BEHAVIOUR: worker daemon thread 'ERIS-LivingUserEpisode', started lazily on the first request; sleeps without timeout when idle, polls every 5 s only while a request is waiting (backoff or user-turn gate). Snapshot = first contiguous same-session run with >=2 rows (keep_tail only for the last run); Gemini runs in a helper thread with join(timeout + 5 s); then episode_store.add; then trim under the lock by (id, timestamp) keys of the snapshot rows only; then optional dream (_dream_saved). Failure (strict): no episode, buffer untouched, failures+=1, next retry min(600, retry_sec*2**(n-1)). Fallback heuristic episode only when the adapter is None or buffer rows >= episode_fallback_rows (also after a Gemini failure/timeout under that pressure). After a commit the worker re-requests itself ('followup') if another non-active-session run with >=2 rows remains. dream() now only calls request_consolidation('dream') when the buffer has >=4 rows.

STATUS KEYS (consolidation_status): pending (new request queued), retry_pending (failed request waiting for backoff), running, worker_alive, failures, next_retry_in_s (0 when failures==0), last_error ('timeout', 'provider_error', ...), last_episode_id, last_duration_ms, last_gemini_ms, lock_wait_ms, lock_wait_max_ms. DEVIATION: the plan said failed requests are re-merged into the pending request; verify check 3(ii) requires status 'pending' to be false after a timeout, so a failed request is parked in a separate retry slot (retry_pending) and merged with new requests when the backoff expires. Trim key is (id, timestamp) rather than id alone so a late duplicate id is not dropped (still only snapshot rows).

TRACE: one living_user_trace.jsonl event kind 'episode_consolidation' per outcome, payload.status in started|committed|empty|failed|deferred with reason, session_id, turn_count, attempt, lock_wait_ms, commit_lock_wait_ms, gemini_ms, duration_ms, episode_id, episode_source, error, failures, retry_in_s.
